overview:
First-term Democrat George Whitesides seeks reelection in a Southern California district that leans Democratic by about six points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised roughly $4 million and holding $2.5 million on hand, while Republican Jason Gibbs has raised under $400,000 with no significant outside support on either side. Prediction markets give Whitesides about a 95% chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's resources, and market pricing. All signs point to a comfortable Whitesides win, though the lack of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
